name: Ironfoot Reclaim Boot (Wide Last)
description: A wide-last boot designed to fit augmented feet with basic chrome or prosthetic extensions — one of the few the Gray Zone-made options that acknowledges not everyone has standard anatomy. The upper is reclaimed leather in irregular browns and blacks, the sole a thick slab of recycled polymer. Sizes are approximate; a cloth tag inside lists three measurements and says 'closest fit wins.'
functionality: Wide last accommodates basic augmented or prosthetic feet. No tech integration.
what_it_says: You've got chrome and you're not hiding it. You also can't afford the Velasca aug-boot, so this is what fits.
story_hooks: Ironfoot's maker keeps a waiting list — demand always exceeds supply, and some names on that list are years old.
A pair fits perfectly, but the person who ordered them never came to collect.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sturdy, deliberately asymmetrical silhouette that reads as utilitarian and uncompromising. The boot sits ankle-high with a pronounced toe box, shaped to accommodate augmented feet without pressure points. Has the honest, assembled-from-salvage appearance of the Gray Zone craftsmanship — no designer pretense, just function.
physical_description.fit: Wide last throughout the foot and instep; compression-resistant to allow for swelling around prosthetic joints and chrome fixtures. The calf opening is generous and unstructured, allowing for easy on-and-off around mechanical components.
physical_description.primary_material: Reclaimed leather (mixed hides stitched together) with visible seams and color variations; thick slab sole of recycled thermopolymer (grey, worn-smooth in patches)
physical_description.texture: Leather is rough, creased, and weathered — some areas show original wear from prior owners, others freshly abraded. Sole has a tactile, slightly grippy surface with visible aggregate trapped in the polymer.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant burnt brown and charcoal black in irregular patches across the upper; sole is industrial grey with darker striations from recycled material blending
physical_description.closures: Heavy-gauge friction laces (salvaged synthetic cord) through eyelets of hammered metal; no hardware branding, just functional fastening
distinctive_features: Visible patchwork construction — seams are part of the aesthetic, not hidden
Oversized toe box with subtle reinforcement stitching to prevent splitting around augmented foot plates
Interior cloth tag hand-printed with three measurement options instead of standardized sizing
Slight cant inward at the heel to accommodate common servo-alignment of lower-leg augmentations
Drainage holes punched near the ankle — explicit acknowledgment that chrome gets wet
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 / the Gray Zone-made — high functionality, zero luxury finish. Accessible price point (Φ40-60 range), designed by and for the augmented underclass
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by dock workers, salvage operators, and chrome-modded residents of ungoverned districts. Signals rejection of corpo fashion standards and comfort with visible modification. Non-judgmental toward augmentation.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn-in from day one — the irregularity is the point. Leather develops deeper creases; sole gradually polishes from use. Some owners patch the uppers with industrial tape or additional leather scraps, creating increasingly unique variations
